title: Predictive Tenant Imbalance Mitigation Guide
author: Claire Nguyen
body:
Summary
-------
This guide describes a predictive, telemetry-driven process for detecting and mitigating tenant imbalance in Redwood Inference (situations where a small number of tenants consume disproportionate shared capacity and risk SLO degradation for other tenants). The playbook ties SLO/error-budget signals to a tenant-priority ledger, automated quarantine, soft-eviction controls, and capacity-synthesis checks so SREs can respond before wide service impact.

Scope
-----
Applies to: multi-tenant inference clusters (hosted API and Dedicated shared clusters).
Excludes: single-tenant Dedicated pools and Private on-prem clusters managed by customer ops (these follow a separate on-prem runbook).

Motivation
----------
- Tenant imbalance causes cascading tail latency and unpredictable burn of cluster-level SLOs.
- Typical symptoms: sudden p99 spikes, KV cache thrashing, model hot-hot partitions, and headroom erosion.
- Reactive eviction causes business disruption; predictive mitigation reduces customer impact and simplifies post-incident remediation.

Key definitions
---------------
- Tenant Imbalance Score (TIS): composite score 0.0–1.0 combining token/sec share, 1m p95 latency delta, model-hotness, and cache miss rate. Threshold: >0.7 = high; 0.9 = critical.
- Priority Ledger: authoritative per-tenant ledger (tier, hard_quota, soft_quota, escalation_policy) used by throttling and eviction controllers.
- Quarantine: temporary rate-limited state with traffic shaping and KV-cache prewarm prevention to protect cluster headroom.

Telemetry & detection
---------------------
Important signals (ingested into SRE telemetry pipeline):
- Per-tenant tokens/sec (1s, 1m, 5m)
- Per-tenant p95/p99 for model endpoints, and delta vs baseline (baseline = 7d rolling median)
- Shared cluster headroom (GPU utilization, model mem pressure, active model instances vs capacity)
- KV cache miss rate and average KV size by tenant
- Error budget burn rate (service-level): 1h and 24h burn windows
- Admission/denial counts from policy gateway

Detection rules (examples):
1) Rapid-share spike: tenant contributes >25% of tokens/sec for a cluster and has >=2x 1m increase vs 5m median => increase TIS by 0.35.
2) Latency correlation: tenant p99 increase >50% and cluster p99 increased >20% in same 60s window => increase TIS by 0.25.
3) Cache thrash: tenant cache miss rate delta >0.15 and model-hotness >0.6 => increase TIS by 0.2.
4) Error-budget coupling: service-level burn rate >12% in last 1h and top-3 tenants account for >60% of requests => mark cluster at-risk and raise alerts.

- Composite TIS calculation occurs each 30s; values persisted for 48h for forensics.

Alerting and early-warning
-------------------------
Severity mapping:
- Warning: TIS >= 0.55 for any tenant (pager to oncall slack channel; playbook runbook flag set).
- Action: TIS >= 0.7 and cluster headroom <15% (pager escalation to SRE oncall and platform product manager).
- Critical: TIS >= 0.9 OR service-level error-budget alarm (automatic emergency mitigation triggers, notify customer-success for affected tenants).

Mitigation playbook (ordered steps)
----------------------------------
1) Observe and validate (SRE oncall)
   - Confirm telemetry via dashboard: tenant TIS, per-tenant token rate, p99 deltas, cache miss rate.
   - Check recent rollouts or deploy windows for potential correlates.
   - If TIS rises due to known customer test activity, annotate and advise customer success.

2) Soft traffic shaping (automated first responder)
   - Apply 5–30% rate reduction to offending tenant(s) using the adaptive throttle controller.
   - Goal: reduce immediate tail while preserving meaningful traffic for the tenant.
   - Continue to monitor TIS over next 60–120s.

3) Quarantine and KV prewarm suppression (automated if shaping insufficient)
   - Move tenant to "quarantine" policy for 5 minutes: stricter rate cap, deprioritized cache population, and connection churn mitigation.
   - Quarantine metrics: fail_rate_target <1%, reduce token/sec by target_pct = min(50%, (TIS-0.7)*100).

4) Priority ledger evaluation and human review
   - Read ledger: tier (e.g., enterprise, standard, free), contractual SLAs, escalation policy.
   - If tenant is tiered enterprise with dedicated escalation, SRE to call product/solutions for coordinated plan.

5) Graceful soft-eviction (manual approval required for high-impact cases)
   - If TIS remains >0.85 after two quarantine cycles and cluster headroom <10%: recommend soft eviction of best-effort tenants (lowest ledger priority).
   - Eviction order policy: (a) fairshare_score, (b) recent error budget consumption, (c) tenant tier.

6) Emergency capacity expansion (if configured)
   - If Dedicated pool supports burst capacity, invoke autoscale-burst with 10–30% additional nodes, and mark capacity-source in incident timeline.

7) Post-mitigation validation and annotation
   - Confirm SLOs returning to baseline for the cluster and top-affected tenants.
   - Annotate incident timeline with causes, actions, time-in-state, and tenant IDs.

Runbook: Rapid Quarantine (for oncall)
-------------------------------------
1) Trigger conditions: TIS >= 0.7 AND (cluster headroom <15% OR service burn >8%/1h).
2) Steps:
   a) Navigate to the "Tenant Imbalance" dashboard.
   b) Click tenant row -> open "Mitigate" -> choose "Soft throttle (30% default)".
   c) Wait 60s, observe TIS trend. If TIS falls below 0.6, remove throttle after 3m.
   d) If TIS remains >0.75 after 2m, escalate to quarantine.
3) Quarantine command (CLI):
   - rctl tenant quarantine --tenant-id=TENANT123 --duration=5m --rate-limit=200rps --kv-populate=deprioritize
4) Rollback: rctl tenant unquarantine --tenant-id=TENANT123

Priority Ledger config (example, YAML)
-------------------------------------
Note: stored in config service; consult change-control for edits.

| tenant_id | tier      | soft_quota_rps | hard_quota_rps | escalation_contact |
|-----------|-----------|----------------|----------------|--------------------|
| TENANT123 | standard  | "500"         | "1500"        | "pm-xyz@redwood.com" |
| TENANT789 | enterprise| "2000"        | "5000"        | "ae-enterprise@redwood.com" |

Example YAML snippet (for automation):

priority_ledger:
  TENANT123:
    tier: standard
    soft_quota_rps: "500"
    hard_quota_rps: "1500"
    escalation_contact: "pm-xyz@redwood.com"

Operational tooling integration
-------------------------------
- Telemetry pipeline: TIS computed by the SLO-synthesis job and emitted to the metrics cluster as metric name: inference.tenant.tis (labels: tenant_id, cluster_id, model_family).
- Controllers: throttle-controller and quarantine-manager read the priority ledger via the config service and enforce via edge policy.
- Simulation harness: use the imbalance-sim CLI to run tenant-mix simulations before making policy changes.

Capacity planning & acceptance criteria
--------------------------------------
- For each multi-tenant cluster, product must provide expected peak tenant share and critical tenants list at onboarding. Onboarding acceptance requires:
  - Headroom target: >= 20% under p95 traffic forecast.
  - Admission rule cookbook: priority ledger entries for top-10 tenants.
- Quarterly exercise: run an "imbalanced surge" simulation (see Simulation section) prior to major model rollouts.

Incident review & RCA standards (for imbalance events)
-----------------------------------------------------
Required artifacts for post-incident review:
1) Timeline: annotated 1s-resolution timeline for 30m before and after mitigation, including operator actions.
2) Telemetry snapshot: per-tenant tokens/sec, p95/p99, cache stats, headroom.
3) Priority ledger state and any changes made during incident.
4) Runbook compliance checklist: were playbook steps followed? If deviation, justify and include alternate remediation.
5) Customer impact statement: list tenant IDs, impact windows, and CS outreach timeline.
6) Regresion test: run simulation with same traffic profile to validate recommended guardrails.

Postmortem scoring rubric (short)
- Detection time: <2m (score pass/fail)
- Time-to-first-mitigation: <5m
- Recovery to baseline SLOs: <15m
- Customer impact: measured in token-loss or error-rates; must be documented

Simulation lab (how to rehearse)
-------------------------------
- Tool: imbalance-sim (part of platform testkit)
- Typical scenario: 3 tenants, 1 heavy attacker at 40x baseline rate, KV sizes skewed.
- Commands: imbalance-sim --scenario=kv-thrash-heavy --duration=15m --metrics-output=/tmp/imb-sim.out
- Acceptance: cluster p99 remains within 1.2x baseline after first automated throttle; SRE should be able to go from alert->quarantine in <3m in simulation.

Escalation & communication
-------------------------
- Notifications: automated Slack message to #sre-incident with tenant id and TIS when action >= quarantine.
- Customer comms: Customer Success should own messaging for enterprise customers after quarantine. Use template: "We observed elevated usage patterns affecting shared latency; we applied temporary controls and are coordinating next steps."

Ownership & SLAs
----------------
- Primary owner: eng-sre (team: tenant-capacity).
- Secondary owner: eng-platform (controllers and ledger).
- Product owner for policy changes: product-infra.
- SLA tie-ins: actions are advisory for standard tier; enforcement may be contractual for free/experimental tiers.

Appendix A — CLI snippets and sample alerts
-------------------------------------------
- Query TIS: rctl metrics query --metric inference.tenant.tis --tenant TENANT123 --since=5m
- Submit ledger change (requires approval): rctl ledger set --tenant=TENANT123 --soft=600 --hard=2000 --approver=product-infra
- Sample Pager alert body (short):
  Title: tenant imbalance high (TENANT123)
  Body: TIS=0.78, tokens/sec=4200 (25% cluster share), cluster_headroom=12%, action=auto-throttle(30%)

Appendix B — Change control and safety checks
----------------------------------------------
- Any change to priority ledger must go through a small-change approval if soft_quota_rps or hard_quota_rps changes >20%.
- Feature flags: quarantine-manager has a kill-switch flag (sre.quarantine.enabled) default true; emergency disable requires two engineer approvals.

Appendix C — Glossary and links
--------------------------------
- TIS: Tenant Imbalance Score (documented above).
- Priority ledger: source-of-truth config service path: /config/priority_ledger
- Related pages: see capacity-onboarding-runway and capacity-observability-and-recovery playbooks.
